name: Thursday
label: Victory
lede: A New Brunswick basement band cut Full Collapse in 20 days, fell out with Victory Records over it, and cost its next label $1.2 million to get free. Then Thursday broke up, spent five years apart while Geoff Rickly fought heroin, and came back.

eras.title: A basement show on New Year's Eve
eras.text: Thursday started among Rutgers students in New Brunswick, New Jersey, and played its first show in the singer's basement. The debut on a small label went unheard, and by 2000 the band had a new guitarist and a Chicago label.

years.h: Geoff Rickly meets Tom Keeley at an Ink & Dagger show
years.p: Keeley and drummer Tucker Rule had already started playing together; Rickly joined months later. Tim Payne on bass and Bill Henderson on guitar make five, all of them Rutgers students.

years.h: Thursday plays its first show in Rickly's basement on New Year's Eve
years.p: The bill in the New Brunswick basement also has [[Midtown|1165d619-d5d5-497e-b1b7-261d1e355d96]], [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]] and [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]].

years.h: Eyeball releases Waiting, and nobody plays it on the radio
years.p: Thursday's debut, still with original guitarist Bill Henderson, comes out on a small New Jersey label with no singles, no radio and no video behind it. A summer demo EP had gone up on MP3.com months earlier.

years.h: Steve Pedulla takes Henderson's guitar, and Victory takes the band
years.p: Thursday leaves Eyeball for Chicago's Victory Records and heads into Big Blue Meenie in Jersey City in November.

eras.title: Full Collapse and whoopee cushions
eras.text: Full Collapse sold 800 copies in its first week and then kept selling. So did Thursday's list of complaints about Victory founder Tony Brummel, which ended in a major-label bidding war.

q: Full Collapse was a record that changed the course and shape of my life.
yt: Understanding in a Car Crash, official video
years.h: Full Collapse sells 800 copies in its first week
years.p: Victory shipped 3,400. Producer Sal Villanueva had cut it in 20 days at Big Blue Meenie, and by October 2008 it had sold 380,000.
years.xp:
The single Understanding in a Car Crash went to college radio in April, and its video, built from live footage, sat in MTV2 rotation for eight weeks. Geoff Rickly has said it's about a car accident involving his girlfriend and his best friend, with a nod to Joy Division. Alternative Press later ranked it No. 10 on its list of the best singles of the 2000s.

Critics split. AbsolutePunk gave the album 95%, Pitchfork 5.6 out of 10, and Rolling Stone's Gavin Edwards heard a band "peeling the scab off endless varieties of pain." It peaked at No. 178 on the Billboard 200. Kerrang!, NME and Rolling Stone later put it among the greatest emo albums.

yt: Understanding in a Car Crash, live, May 2001
years.h: Thursday spends summer 2001 on Warped Tour
years.p: Full Collapse is a few months old and the band is on its first Warped Tour.

years.h: Victory has Thursday whoopee cushions made without asking
years.p: Victory staff produced Thursday-branded whoopee cushions to promote Full Collapse, without the band's consent. They were dropped after Thursday objected.
years.xp:
When Geoff Rickly took it up with Tony Brummel, the Victory founder reportedly said the label "was a big company and that they didn't have time to run everything by the band."

It wasn't the first argument. Brummel had insisted on a cheaper one-page insert without printed lyrics instead of the booklet the band wanted, and a compromise was eventually reached. Thursday later said the relationship "was based entirely on numbers."

years.h: Thursday tells its own fans to skip Five Stories Falling
years.p: The Victory EP was a contractual obligation, and the band said so from the stage. Tony Brummel had also pushed back on what the Full Collapse artwork cost.
years.xp: By Thursday's account, the label's dismissive attitude nearly broke the band up. Five Stories Falling was what was left to deliver.

years.big: "When we parted ways with Victory, we got our asses kicked."
years.src: Wikipedia: Thursday (band) · Wikipedia: Victory Records · Wikipedia: Full Collapse
years.h: Island Def Jam wins a bidding war for Thursday
years.p: Geoff Rickly, on the split. Island paid Victory $1.2 million for its claim on two more albums, after a May 2002 statement in which Thursday said Tony Brummel's interest was all sales, no art.
years.xp:
The deal was announced in late May 2002 and made official on September 9, once the exit terms were settled. Rickly said the band would be paying off that bill for as long as it was on the new label, and the Victory logo had to appear on Thursday's next two records.

Relations later thawed. Thursday's Kill the House Lights DVD says Brummel and Victory welcomed the band back with open arms. By then Full Collapse had sold 111,000 copies.

years.h: The Plea for Peace Tour starts as the Island paperwork clears
years.p: Thursday headlines the run in September and October, then starts writing the next record in mid-November.

years.h: Rickly takes the producer's chair for [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]]
years.p: He produces I Brought You My Bullets, You Brought Me Your Love, the New Jersey band's debut. My Chemical Romance later named Thursday as an influence.

eras.title: A Top 10 debut, then a break
eras.text: Thursday's first Island record opened at No. 7, and tours with AFI, Deftones and Thrice followed. By 2004 label pressure, the road and health problems had the band stepping off.

years.src: Wikipedia: War All the Time (Thursday album) · Wikipedia: Thursday (band)
years.h: War All the Time opens at No. 7 on the Billboard 200
years.p: It sold 74,000 copies in its first week for Thursday's Island debut, made over six months in Jersey City and a Massachusetts farmhouse. Andrew Everding plays keyboards on seven tracks; he's made an official member in December 2004.
years.xp:
Two videos tell the story. The Signals Over the Air video, directed by Joakim Åhlund, came out August 28, 2003. The War All the Time video, shot with infrared and green night-vision filters, used a fake news feed that looked real, and MTV banned it.

Rickly said the album wasn't political: he was "speaking about love being a war." Entertainment Weekly's Greg Kot heard a record "sensitive as a teardrop, but hitting with the impact of a two-by-four across the jaw." It had sold 259,000 copies by April 2004, with a fall tour of Thrice and Coheed and Cambria and then Deftones into December.

years.src: Wikipedia: War All the Time (Thursday album) · Wikipedia: Thursday (band)
years.h: Thursday steps off the road
years.p: The band cites label pressure, relentless touring and health problems. Geoff Rickly has epilepsy, which has affected Thursday's touring.
years.xp: It had been a full year: Japan in January, AFI in February and March, Warped Tour in April, and The Cure on a US tour in July and August.

years.h: Thursday comes back for CBGB, live on the club's website
years.p: The August 25 show is a benefit for the Bowery club, then fighting to keep its lease.

years.h: A City by the Light Divided, with Dave Fridmann at the board
years.p: The first Thursday album not produced by Sal Villanueva, and the last for Island, which the band left early in 2007.
years.xp:
Rickly built the title from two lines of Octavio Paz's poem "Sunstone." The album streamed on MySpace on April 18, two weeks before release, and spun off two singles, Counting 5-4-3-2-1 and At This Velocity.

Five demos for it were stolen in fall 2005 from the iPod of My American Heart's tour manager. After Island, Ferret, Atlantic and Fueled by Ramen all showed interest.
play: A City by the Light Divided

eras.title: Epitaph, then a full stop
eras.text: Thursday signed to Epitaph in 2008, headlined a Taste of Chaos tour that Tom Keeley called an awful experience, and made one more album with Dave Fridmann. In November 2011 it announced it was stopping, and Rickly later said hiatus was the wrong word.

years.h: Common Existence lands on Epitaph
years.p: Thursday signed to Epitaph Records on September 30, 2008, and headlined the 2009 Taste of Chaos tour behind this album.
years.xp:
Rickly said the title refers to "humanity's shared experience" and that "almost every song on the record is connected to a different writer," among them Denis Johnson, Martin Amis, Roberto Bolano and David Foster Wallace.

Taste of Chaos, with Bring Me the Horizon, Four Year Strong, Pierce the Veil and Cancer Bats, went less well. Keeley estimated about 90% of audiences left before Thursday played, and Rickly called the tour "stupid."

years.cap: Thursday at Kool Haus, Toronto, July 22, 2011
years.h: No Devolución is the last record of the first run
years.p: Thursday's sixth album was cut with Dave Fridmann at Tarbox Road Studios in Fredonia, New York. Geoff Rickly called it a radical departure in style but "a return" in substance.

years.h: "So, we stop. For now, at least."
years.p: Thursday's November 22 statement said personal circumstances made it impossible to continue in the spirit that made the band special. In January 2013 Geoff Rickly said they had in fact disbanded.
years.xp: Rickly told it plainly in 2013: hiatus was the wrong word, used only in case the band ever played shows again. No new material, he said, would be made.

years.h: Thursday plays its last show at Soundwave in Perth
years.p: On March 5 the original run ends at a festival in Australia, on the far side of the world from New Brunswick.

eras.title: Five years apart
eras.text: The members scattered into other bands. Rickly was mugged in New York, poisoned and robbed in Hamburg, and cut ties with the investor behind his label, Martin Shkreli. The reunion is what he credits with pulling him out of heroin.

years.h: Rickly is mugged in New York
years.p: His phone, iPad, wallet, credit card, rent money and medication are taken. He told Spin in 2017 that his heroin addiction began shortly after the breakup.
years.xp: Two years later, touring with No Devotion for the Reeperbahn Festival, he was poisoned and robbed in Hamburg. He was hospitalized and played Paris the next day.

years.h: Rickly starts No Devotion with ex-Lostprophets members
years.p: He also keeps his United Nations project going. Meanwhile Tucker Rule tours as a drummer with The Wanted and [[Yellowcard|3630fff3-52fc-4e97-ab01-d68fd88e4135]].

years.h: Martin Shkreli turns out to be bankrolling Rickly's label
years.p: Collect Records, founded by Geoff Rickly in 2009, had the pharma executive as a silent investor. Rickly cut ties within two days, and the label lost its funding.
years.xp: According to reports, Shkreli had bought a guitar of Rickly's from the Full Collapse era for $10,000, which is how they met. Leaving cost the label about "a million dollars" in backing.

years.h: Five years after "we stop," Thursday books Wrecking Ball
years.p: Announced in March for August in Atlanta. Geoff Rickly said the band had reconciled its differences after five years of barely speaking, and the reunion helped him get clean.
years.xp:
In January the members had posted a photo together on Rickly's Twitter. He called it "mending some fences and healing some old wounds." The show, he said, would be the lineup that began touring on Full Collapse.

The band agreed to play only two days before announcing, swayed by the festival's lineup and its charity ties.

years.h: Starland Ballroom gets its homecoming on December 30
years.p: Back at the Sayreville, New Jersey club where Andrew Everding became an official member in December 2004. Announced in June.

eras.title: Signals over the air, again
eras.text: The reunion was meant to end in 2019 and didn't. Thursday opened for My Chemical Romance, streamed three shows, played its records front to back, swapped two founders for touring players and, in 2024, released its first new song in 13 years.

years.cap: Thursday at McCarren Park, Brooklyn, Northside Festival, c. 2017
years.h: Thursday headlines Northside Festival in Brooklyn
years.p: June comes weeks after a 24-date spring tour, announced in January, the first full run since 2012.

years.h: Thursday says goodbye at Saint Vitus, then keeps playing
years.p: The reunion was set to end in 2019. International fans pushed back, and the band added a Cologne festival in May, Eindhoven, and two London nights in December: Full Collapse on the first, War All the Time on the second.
years.xp: Announcing the end in October 2018, the band wrote: "When we stopped playing last time, it wasn't on the best of terms." This time, it said, it would put down touring on the very highest of notes.

years.h: [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]] brings Thursday on for its first show back
years.p: On December 20 at The Shrine in Los Angeles. Geoff Rickly had produced the band's debut in 2002.
years.xp: It turned into a run. In September 2022 Thursday opened seven North American dates for My Chemical Romance, and on the last night played Jet Black New Year with Gerard Way. Rickly then sang This Is the Best Day Ever with My Chemical Romance.

years.h: Thursday plays Signals to a camera
years.p: From August 2020 to April 2021 the band streams three Signals shows, with guests including [[Frank Iero|358db9a2-3c78-4afb-93b5-d18b34b86eab]], [[Jim Ward|da9ed660-3aef-4c2d-bcc0-89e512696baf]], [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] and Bartees Strange.
years.xp: The first was stripped back with Iero. The second was a holiday show with all four guests. The third played Full Collapse and No Devolución in full.

years.cap: Geoff Rickly at Starland Ballroom, Sayreville, February 27, 2022
years.h: Norman Brannon and Stu Richardson take over for Keeley and Payne
years.p: Thursday is now Geoff Rickly, Steve Pedulla and Tucker Rule, with [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]]'s Brannon and No Devotion's Richardson touring. In July they headline Philadelphia's This Is Hardcore, playing Full Collapse in full.

years.h: Rickly publishes the novel Someone Who Isn't Me
years.p: An autofictional account of his heroin addiction and experimental psychedelic treatment with ibogaine, from Rose Books.

years.h: The first new Thursday song in 13 years
years.p: Application for Release From the Dream arrives April 12. White Bikes, recorded at Hansa Studio in Berlin and about the death of a friend of Rickly's, follows December 6.
years.xp: Stu Richardson produced the first song and played keyboards on it; it's the first with Norman Brannon on guitar. A third song, Taking Inventory of a Frozen Lake, followed January 1, 2025.

years.h: The Full City Devolución tour ends in Boston
years.p: It marks Full Collapse at 25, A City by the Light Divided at 20 and No Devolución at 15, with [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]]'s Chris Conley along. The last date is April 30.
years.xp: In February the band was also announced for Louder Than Life in Louisville in September.
